issue.title: Bug: system-health.service takes 90s to stop during cold reboot

failure.body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

High

### Description of the bug

PR #24656 changed MonitorSystemBusTask and Sysmonitor from ProcessTaskBase to ThreadTaskBase to reduce memory footprint. This change inadvertently removed the kill() call that previously terminated the GLib.MainLoop subprocess immediately, causing system-health.service to always time out during shutdown and adding ~90 seconds to every cold reboot.
Affected versions: All platforms, all builds after this PR was merged.

### Steps to Reproduce

Run cold reboot or run "systemctl stop system-health.service"

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

system-health.service always times out during shutdown, which adds approximately 90 seconds to each cold reboot.

### Relevant log output

```shell
2026 Apr 14 <IPV6>.047020 sonic INFO    systemd[1]: Stopping system-health.service - SONiC system health monitor...
2026 Apr 14 <IPV6>.240603 sonic WARNING systemd[1]: system-health.service: State 'stop-sigterm' timed out. Killing.
```

### Output of `show version`, `show techsupport`

```shell

```

### Attach files (if any)

_No response_

resolution.title: [system-health] Fix 90s stop timeout during cold reboot and system-health.service stop
resolution.description:
Fixes #26754 by ensuring GLib.MainLoop() is cleanly quit when stopping the MonitorSystemBusTask thread.

### Testing (202605)

#### system-health.service takes 90s to stop during cold reboot (#26754)
**Without fix**
Run `systemctl stop system-health.service` then in syslog:
```
2026 Jul 29 <IPV6>.919542 strtk5-7260-01 NOTICE healthd[20798]: Caught SIGTERM - exiting...
2026 Jul 29 <IPV6>.919885 strtk5-7260-01 INFO systemd[1]: Stopping system-health.service - SONiC system health monitor...
2026 Jul 29 <IPV6>.047726 strtk5-7260-01 WARNING systemd[1]: system-health.service: State 'stop-sigterm' timed out. Killing.
2026 Jul 29 <IPV6>.047889 strtk5-7260-01 NOTICE systemd[1]: system-health.service: Killing process 20798 (healthd) with signal SIGKILL.
2026 Jul 29 <IPV6>.048016 strtk5-7260-01 NOTICE systemd[1]: system-health.service: Killing process 20802 (healthd) with signal SIGKILL.
2026 Jul 29 <IPV6>.060972 strtk5-7260-01 WARNING systemd[1]: system-health.service: Main process exited, code=killed, status=9/KILL
2026 Jul 29 <IPV6>.061306 strtk5-7260-01 WARNING systemd[1]: system-health.service: Failed with result 'timeout'.
2026 Jul 29 <IPV6>.062419 strtk5-7260-01 INFO systemd[1]: Stopped system-health.service - SONiC system health monitor.
2026 Jul 29 <IPV6>.063224 strtk5-7260-01 INFO systemd[1]: system-health.service: Consumed 2.915s CPU time, 66.7M memory peak.
```
~90s to stop

**With Fix**
Run `systemctl stop system-health.service` then in syslog:
```
2026 Jul 29 <IPV6>.912552 strtk5-7260-01 INFO systemd[1]: Stopping system-health.service - SONiC system health monitor...
2026 Jul 29 <IPV6>.081462 strtk5-7260-01 INFO systemd[1]: system-health.service: Deactivated successfully.
2026 Jul 29 <IPV6>.081729 strtk5-7260-01 INFO systemd[1]: Stopped system-health.service - SONiC system health monitor.
2026 Jul 29 <IPV6>.082306 strtk5-7260-01 INFO systemd[1]: system-health.service: Consumed 7.016s CPU time, 67.1M memory peak
```
~1-2s to stop

#### Fast-reboot shutdown increase
Fix for issue described in PR https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/pull/26386

**Without Fix**
Run `fast-reboot` then in syslog:
```
2026 Jul 28 <IPV6>.720942 strtk5-7260-01 NOTICE root: Starting fast-reboot
...
2026 Jul 28 <IPV6>.638271 strtk5-7260-01 INFO kernel: [    0.000000] Command line: reboot=p console=ttyS0...
```
207.917 seconds total from starting fast-reboot to the first kernel log on the boot side.

**With Fix**
Run `fast-reboot` then in syslog:
```
2026 Jul 29 <IPV6>.563157 strtk5-7260-01 NOTICE root: Starting fast-reboot
...
2026 Jul 29 <IPV6>.781422 strtk5-7260-01 INFO kernel: [    0.000000] Command line: reboot=p console=ttyS0...
```
111.218 seconds total from starting fast-reboot to the first kernel log on the boot side.
